section: Advent of Europeans - Portuguese, Dutch, English, French and Danish
subsections: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters
Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin
European settlements in Andhra - company and grant

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of the Portuguese Estado da India?
o: A private joint-stock company controlled by a Court of Directors
A sovereign trading corporation created by the States-General of the Netherlands
A religious order operating under the Danish Crown
A state-controlled organisation administering Portuguese possessions in India
accepted.x: The Portuguese Estado da India was state-controlled, unlike the private English and Dutch joint-stock companies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the organisational nature of the companies rather than their trading activity.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Dutch East India Company, established in 1602, was granted which of the following powers by the States-General?
o: Sovereign powers such as waging war, building forts and making treaties
Exclusive authority to mint coins throughout Asia
The power to appoint Mughal governors in coastal provinces
Only the right to collect customs duties in Indian ports
accepted.x: The States-General granted the VOC sovereign powers, including making war, constructing forts and concluding treaties.
accepted.tq: Match the company with the distinctive authority granted to it.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the European trading companies in India:
1. The Dutch established their first factory at Masulipatnam in 1605.
2. The Danish established their first factory at Tranquebar in 1620.
3. The French established their first factory at Surat in 1668.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Masulipatnam was the Dutch first factory in 1605, Tranquebar was the Danish first factory in 1620, and Surat was the French first factory in 1668.
accepted.tq: Test several company–factory–year pairs together, watching for swapped establishments.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters in 1610, later being replaced by Nagapatnam. The French headquarters was Pondicherry, while Tranquebar was the initial Danish headquarters.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive headquarters fact and eliminate swapped locations.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following European companies in the chronological order of their formation:
A. French East India Company
B. English East India Company
C. Danish East India Company
D. Dutch East India Company
accepted.x: The companies were formed in the order English (1600), Dutch (1602), Danish (1616) and French (1664).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest company first and then compare the close years 1600 and 1602.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The headquarters of the French possessions in India was located at
accepted.x: Pondicherry served as the headquarters of the French settlements in India.
accepted.tq: Test the principal headquarters rather than the first factory.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the English East India Company is correct?
o: It was established by the States-General of the Netherlands in 1602.
Its charter was issued by Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
It was a state-controlled Portuguese organisation.
Its original charter gave it legislative authority over all Indian territories.
accepted.x: Elizabeth I granted the English East India Company its charter on 31 December 1600. The charter granted trading privileges, not territorial or legislative authority.
accepted.tq: Use the charter date and distinguish trading privileges from territorial powers.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The original charter of the English East India Company provided a monopoly of trade with the East Indies for
accepted.x: The original charter granted the English East India Company a 15-year monopoly of East Indies trade, which was later made perpetual.
accepted.tq: Separate the initial charter period from the later perpetual arrangement.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who obtained the site for Madras from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George in 1639?
accepted.x: Francis Day obtained the site from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George at Madras in 1639.
accepted.tq: Apply the founder–work trap by distinguishing Francis Day from Job Charnock.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the early English settlements:
1. Job Charnock established the English settlement at Sutanuti in 1690.
2. The zamindari rights over Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata were bought in 1698.
3. Fort William was built at Calcutta in 1700.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690; the three zamindaris were bought in 1698, and Fort William was built in 1700.
accepted.tq: Check the sequence of settlement, acquisition of zamindaris and fort construction.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rival English companies were merged in 1707 into the
o: United Company of the East Indies
accepted.x: In 1707, the rival English companies merged into the United Company of Merchants.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact official name rather than a descriptive substitute.
accepted.sec: European companies - formation, charter, first factory, headquarters  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who formulated the Blue Water Policy in Portuguese India?
accepted.x: Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese viceroy in India, followed the Blue Water Policy, which emphasised naval mastery rather than territorial expansion inland.
accepted.tq: Use the governor–policy association and distinguish naval control from land conquest.
accepted.sec: Portuguese governors - policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with Afonso de Albuquerque?
o: Capture of Goa from Bijapur in 1510
Transfer of the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530
Abolition of Sati in Portuguese territories
accepted.x: Nuno da Cunha moved the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530. Albuquerque captured Goa, encouraged mixed marriages and abolished Sati.
accepted.tq: Find the deed belonging to another governor rather than the principal governor named.
accepted.sec: Portuguese governors - policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Nuno da Cunha’s role in Portuguese India?
o: He moved the headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530.
He founded the Dutch VOC at Pulicat.
He introduced the Blue Water Policy in 1505.
He established the French headquarters at Pondicherry.
accepted.x: Nuno da Cunha shifted the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530 and obtained Diu and Bassein from Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Match the governor with the administrative change associated with him.
accepted.sec: Portuguese governors - policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Portuguese cartaz system was primarily a system of
accepted.x: Cartaz was a naval-pass system used to regulate shipping and enforce the Portuguese maritime monopoly, along with convoys and customs duties.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical function of an unfamiliar administrative term from its context.
accepted.sec: Portuguese governors - policy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who helped Vasco da Gama in navigating from the East African coast to Calicut in 1498?
accepted.x: Vasco da Gama was piloted with the help of the trader Abdul Majid on his voyage to Calicut.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the navigator’s helper from later company officials and commanders.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut on 17 May 1498 after following which route?
o: Lisbon–Cape of Good Hope–East African coast–Calicut
accepted.x: The voyage proceeded from Lisbon around the Cape of Good Hope along the East African coast to Calicut.
accepted.tq: Arrange the geographical stages of the voyage in their actual sequence.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many ships accompanied Vasco da Gama on his first voyage that reached Calicut in 1498?
accepted.x: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut with three ships: Sao Gabriel, Sao Rafael and Berrio.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical detail and verify it against the associated named list.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains the ships of Vasco da Gama’s first voyage to Calicut?
o: Sao Gabriel, Sao Rafael and Berrio
Sao Rafael, Flor de la Mar and Berrio
Sao Gabriel, Red Dragon and Santa Maria
accepted.x: The three ships were Sao Gabriel, Sao Rafael and Berrio.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure ship name and eliminate lists containing vessels from other voyages or traditions.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At the time of Vasco da Gama’s arrival at Calicut in 1498, the ruler of Calicut was the
accepted.x: The Hindu ruler of Calicut, known as the Zamorin or Samuthiri, welcomed Vasco da Gama in 1498.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the local ruler at Calicut from rulers of inland Deccan states.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Vasco da Gama’s second voyage is correct?
o: The Zamorin accepted his trading terms and granted him Goa.
He attacked Calicut after the Zamorin refused trade and settled at Kochi.
He established the French factory at Surat.
accepted.x: During the second voyage in 1502, the Zamorin refused trade; Vasco da Gama attacked Calicut and settled at Kochi. He died at Kochi in 1524.
accepted.tq: Separate the first voyage from the second voyage and its consequences.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the political situation in 1498 is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Manuel I was the ruler of Portugal in 1498. Sikandar Lodi ruled Delhi, and Immadi Narasimha Raya was the ruler of Vijayanagara at that time.
accepted.tq: Match rulers with their regions and watch for famous but chronologically unsuitable names.
accepted.sec: Vasco da Gama - route, arrival, Zamorin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following French settlements was established in 1731?
accepted.x: Yanam was established by the French in 1731. Mahe and Karaikal were established in 1725 and 1739 respectively.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the close eighteenth-century dates of French settlements.
accepted.sec: French settlements - order of establishment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Pondicherry was established in 1674, with the grant dating to 1673. Chandernagore is associated with 1673 in the settlement chronology.
accepted.tq: Check the year against the settlement sequence and identify the displaced date.
accepted.sec: French settlements - order of establishment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the Battle of Wandiwash in 1760, which combination represents the French settlements that remained in India?
o: Madras, Bombay, Calcutta, Tranquebar and Pulicat
Surat, Masulipatnam, Goa, Daman and Diu
Pondicherry, Calicut, Cochin, Bassein and Hormuz
Pondicherry, Karaikal, Yanam, Mahe and Chandernagore
accepted.x: After Eyre Coote defeated Count de Lally at Wandiwash, the French retained Pondicherry, Karaikal, Yanam, Mahe and Chandernagore.
accepted.tq: Use the post-war survival list and avoid mixing French settlements with Portuguese or English possessions.
accepted.sec: French settlements - order of establishment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who defeated Count de Lally at the Battle of Wandiwash in 1760?
accepted.x: Eyre Coote defeated the French commander Count de Lally at Wandiwash in 1760.
accepted.tq: Apply the commander–battle trap by distinguishing Eyre Coote from Robert Clive.
accepted.sec: French settlements - order of establishment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding European settlements in Andhra is correct?
o: Nizampatnam was exclusively a Portuguese settlement.
Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement in North Coastal Andhra.
Yanam was a Danish settlement on the Coromandel coast.
Pulicat was established as the French headquarters in Andhra.
accepted.x: Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement in North Coastal Andhra. Yanam was French, while Nizampatnam and Pulicat were associated with more than one European power.
accepted.tq: Use the place–company association and reject one-company simplifications.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of European control at Nizampatnam?
accepted.x: Nizampatnam was first associated with the Dutch and later with the English, who were present there by 1611.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of control rather than merely identifying one company.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pulicat was important in the European trade network because it was
o: the English capital of the Madras Presidency
the French headquarters and a centre for indigo
a Portuguese settlement captured by the Dutch and later their headquarters
the Danish headquarters after the acquisition of Serampore
accepted.x: Pulicat was initially Portuguese, was captured by the Dutch and became the Dutch headquarters in 1610; pepper and cloth were important commodities there.
accepted.tq: Combine the place, change of control, headquarters and commodities clues.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Golden Farman of 1636 granting English trade concessions was issued by
accepted.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda issued the Golden Farman in 1636, granting trade concessions to the English.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–grant association and distinguish Golconda from neighbouring Deccan powers.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Portuguese were called Budata Keechu by local people. Bangaru Farmana was the Golden Farman, and Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters.
accepted.tq: Test the local name and distinguish it from the grant and headquarters terms.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The influence of the Portuguese in Andhra declined by the mid-seventeenth century mainly because
o: their religious intolerance alienated the rulers of Golconda
they abandoned maritime trade in favour of agriculture
the French prohibited their entry into the Coromandel ports
the Danish captured all their Andhra settlements
accepted.x: Portuguese influence declined by the mid-seventeenth century because religious intolerance alienated the rulers of Golconda.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated cause-and-effect relationship rather than a military explanation.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was introduced in India by the Portuguese?
accepted.x: Tobacco was among the crops introduced into India by the Portuguese. Other listed crops are not included in this group of Portuguese introductions.
accepted.tq: Recognise a crop contribution and avoid importing unrelated colonial crops.
accepted.sec: Portuguese contributions - crops, printing press  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following crops:
1. Chilli
2. Maize
3. Cashew
4. Groundnut
Which of the crops given above were introduced into India by the Portuguese?
accepted.x: Chilli, maize, cashew and groundnut were all included among the crops introduced into India by the Portuguese.
accepted.tq: Test a complete crop list and avoid excluding less commonly recalled items.
accepted.sec: Portuguese contributions - crops, printing press  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first printing press in India was introduced by the Portuguese at Goa in
accepted.x: The Portuguese introduced the printing press at Goa in 1556.
accepted.tq: Separate the printing-press year from the arrival, Goa-capture and English-charter years.
accepted.sec: Portuguese contributions - crops, printing press  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of Portuguese presence in India?
o: First to arrive, first to leave; Goa was freed in 1947
First to arrive, last to leave; Goa, Daman and Diu were freed in 1961
Last to arrive, first to leave; Goa was freed in 1956
First to arrive, last to leave; Goa was freed in 1971
accepted.x: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to arrive and the last colonial power to leave India. Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated in 1961 through Operation Vijay.
accepted.tq: Combine the arrival–departure comparison with the precise liberation year.
accepted.sec: Portuguese contributions - crops, printing press  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following commodities was specifically associated with Pulicat in the European trade network?
accepted.x: Pepper and cloth were important commodities traded through Pulicat.
accepted.tq: Match the port with its characteristic commodities rather than its political controller.
accepted.sec: European settlements in Andhra - company and grant  [APPSC]
